contract_md:
- **POST-1** The input gives an integer \(1 \le N \le 100\) and exactly \(N\) rows of \(N\) characters. An ASCII lowercase letter at row \(i\), column \(j\) labels one directed edge from \(i\) to \(j\). A hyphen indicates no edge. Self-loops are allowed.
- **POST-2** The output contains \(N\) rows of \(N\) decimal integers. Entry \((i,j)\) answers the ordered pair from vertex \(i\) to vertex \(j\).
- **POST-3** Each entry is \(-1\) exactly when no palindrome-labeled walk exists. Otherwise it is the minimum number of edges in such a walk. Walks may repeat vertices and edges. Every finite answer is at most \(2N^2-1\).
- **POST-4** Every diagonal entry is \(0\) because the empty walk is a palindrome. An off-diagonal entry is \(1\) exactly when its directed edge exists.
- **POST-5** With distinct endpoints and no direct edge, a two-edge walk with equal labels forces an answer of \(2\). If no such walk exists, the answer cannot be \(2\). Any finite answer of at least \(2\) requires a common label on an edge leaving the start and an edge entering the end.
- **POST-6** Applying a bijection to the edge labels preserves the entire output matrix.
- **POST-7** The program must handle \(N=100\), including dense graphs and graphs whose shortest qualifying walks revisit vertices many times. Reading the matrix and writing all answers each require at least \(\Omega(N^2)\) work.

isolation.mechanism: hardened isolated codex exec (empty tmpdir, read-only, tool flags disabled, credentials stripped, full event-lifecycle audit including item.started)
